name: @material-tax-reporting/tax-domain
description: Tax-year-versioned Canada and Ontario annual personal tax calculations for local return preparation; not filing software.
//: Nothing imports this package yet. '@material-tax-reporting/tax-domain'
appears nowhere in apps/, packages/ or scripts/ as an import specifier, and
neither workflow builds it. The entry below is therefore written for the
consumer that does not exist yet, and the trap it replaces is named here so
the next person does not rediscover it.
What was here before: 'main', 'types' and the '.' entry all named
'./dist/*', and the build script was 'tsc -p tsconfig.json'. TypeScript is
not a dependency of this repository or of any workspace, and no compiler is
installed, so that script could not run. ./dist does not exist and is
git-ignored, so every consumer would have failed on a file nothing produces:
Node with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming dist/index.js, and a bundler with its
own unresolved-import error for that same path.
The entry now names TypeScript source, which a bundler reads directly, as
the documentation site and the desktop renderer already do for
packages/surface-kernel. There is deliberately no 'node' condition and no
build script: nothing Node-direct consumes this package, and a build step
nothing runs is a build step nobody maintains.
THE TRAP, if you are the first to import this from a file Node executes
directly: this entry cannot work for you, and no Node upgrade will change
that. Node refuses to strip types for any file under node_modules at every
version, and a workspace package is reached through a node_modules link, so
importing it by name fails with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING
even on a Node new enough to strip types elsewhere (verified on 26.4.0, with
and without --experimental-strip-types). On the 22.13.0 and 22.14.0 the
workflows pin, which strip nothing at all, the same import fails earlier as
ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION. This is exactly why surface-kernel ships a
compiled ./dist rather than relying on a newer runtime.
So do not 'fix' it by bumping Node or adding a strip-types flag. Copy
packages/surface-kernel instead: add a 'node' condition naming
./dist/index.js, add scripts/build.mjs that transpiles with esbuild (never
tsc, which type-checks and so could withhold a release), add esbuild to
devDependencies AND regenerate package-lock.json in the same commit because
npm ci refuses a manifest the lockfile does not match, and add a 'prebuild'
hook in the consuming workspace exactly as apps/desktop already does for
surface-kernel.
Relative specifiers inside src/ end in '.ts', matching surface-kernel. They
used to end in '.js', the form tsc wants under NodeNext, which nothing here
runs. Node's type stripping does not rewrite '.js' to '.ts' (verified), so
those specifiers made src/ unloadable by Node by path as well as by package
name -- which is the form a test suite in this package would use, as
surface-kernel's 'node --test --experimental-strip-types' script does.
esbuild does perform that rewrite, so the old specifiers did not break the
bundler; this constraint comes from Node alone.
